items.a: A hosted uptime monitoring platform built around the open-source Uptime Kuma engine. You sign up, add your sites and get alerts, with nothing to install or maintain.

items.q: Do I need a credit card to start?
items.a: No. The Free plan needs no card. The Pro trial also starts without payment details being charged until the trial ends; cancel before then and you pay nothing.

items.q: How is this different from self-hosting Uptime Kuma?
items.a: Self-hosting gives you full control but also the upkeep: updates, backups, SSL and the risk of monitoring from the same server you are watching. We run all of that for you.

items.q: How often are my sites checked?
items.a: Every 3 minutes on Free, every minute on Pro and every 30 seconds on Business.

items.q: Can I publish a status page for my customers?
items.a: Yes. Every account gets a status page on our subdomain, and Pro and Business can use their own custom domain.

items.q: Can I change or cancel my plan?
items.a: Yes, at any time from your billing page. Upgrades apply immediately and cancellations take effect at the end of the billing period.
Yes. See our refund policy for the 14-day refund window.

items.q: Where is my data stored and is it GDPR compliant?
items.a: We are a UK company and handle personal data under UK and EU GDPR. A data processing agreement and our list of sub-processors are available on request.

items.q: Can I delete my account and data?
items.a: Yes. You can delete your account from settings, which removes your monitors and monitoring data.

Compare.disclaimer: Comparison is based on publicly available information and may change. Please check each provider's website for current details.

better-stack.name: Better Stack
better-stack.headline: A lightweight Better Stack alternative for uptime monitoring
better-stack.intro: Better Stack bundles monitoring with logs, incident management and on-call scheduling. If you only need dependable uptime checks and a status page, a focused tool can be simpler and cheaper.
theyGood: Broad platform: uptime, logs and incident management in one place
weGood: Simple, low-priced plans aimed at individuals and small teams
Built on open-source Uptime Kuma, with no lock-in to a closed engine
Focus on uptime checks, alerts and status pages only

rows.label: Best for
rows.them: Teams that need on-call and logs

better-stack.chooseThem: you need on-call rotations, log management or advanced incident workflows.
better-stack.chooseUs: you want straightforward uptime checks, alerts and a status page at a low monthly price.

uptimerobot.name: UptimeRobot
uptimerobot.headline: An UptimeRobot alternative built on open-source Uptime Kuma
uptimerobot.intro: UptimeRobot is a long-established uptime monitor. If you want an open-source engine, faster checks on small plans and a modern interface, we are worth a look.
theyGood: Long track record and a large user base
weGood: Open-source engine you could move to self-hosting later
Fast check intervals on affordable paid plans

rows.label: Self-hosting option
rows.us: Yes, the engine is open source

rows.label: Best for
rows.them: Anyone wanting a familiar, established tool

uptimerobot.chooseThem: you prefer a long-established service and its existing free tier fits your needs.
uptimerobot.chooseUs: you value an open-source engine and modern, low-priced paid plans.

cronitor.name: Cronitor
cronitor.headline: A Cronitor alternative for website and API uptime
cronitor.intro: Cronitor is strong at monitoring cron jobs and scheduled tasks. If your main goal is checking that websites and APIs are reachable, a dedicated uptime tool fits more directly.
weGood: Website, API, port and ping monitoring
cronitor.chooseThem: your main need is watching cron jobs and background tasks.
cronitor.chooseUs: your main need is knowing when your sites and APIs are down.

uptime-kuma.name: self-hosted Uptime Kuma
uptime-kuma.headline: Self-hosted Uptime Kuma vs hosted: which should you choose?
uptime-kuma.intro: Uptime Kuma is excellent software, and we use it as our engine. The question is whether you want to run it yourself or let us do it.
theyGood: Full control over your data and configuration
No subscription cost beyond your own server
weGood: No servers, updates, backups or SSL renewals to manage
Monitoring from infrastructure separate from your own
Managed status pages, alerts and billing in one place

rows.label: Independence from your servers
rows.them: Depends on where you host it

uptime-kuma.chooseThem: you enjoy running your own infrastructure and want complete control.
uptime-kuma.chooseUs: you would rather spend your time on your product than on keeping a monitor alive.
